headline: Margins expand and EPS surges as buybacks trim share count
summary_short: DaVita's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 4.1% q/q and 5.2% y/y to $3.554B, while diluted EPS climbed to $4.02 (+40.1% q/q, +55.8% y/y) as operating margin expanded to 16.3% from 14.1% q/q.
summary_long: Revenue grew 4.1% q/q and 5.2% y/y to $3.554B, driven by payor mix shifts and typical annual rate increases, partly offset by seasonal co-insurance impact. Operating margin expanded to 16.3% from 14.1% q/q as patient care costs per treatment fell on lower payroll taxes and pharmaceutical costs, partly offset by higher health benefits expense; G&A rose on professional fees. Diluted EPS rose to $4.02 from $2.87 q/q and $2.58 y/y, helped by a smaller share count after $348M of quarterly buybacks. Free cash flow was $256M, up from $157M y/y. Cash fell 5.6% y/y to $669.0M as buybacks and debt paydown offset proceeds from a $500M term loan. FY2026 guidance: adjusted operating income $2,150-$2,250M, adjusted diluted EPS $14.10-$15.20, FCF $1,000-$1,250M.

drivers.explanation: Quarter change driven by payor mix shifts and normal fluctuations, partly offset by seasonal co-insurance/deductible impact and a rate increase; year-to-date change driven by typical annual increases including the Medicare base rate, partly offset by payor mix.

Per-treatment patient care costs fell q/q on lower payroll taxes and pharmaceutical costs plus favorable fixed-cost leverage from higher treatment volume, partly offset by higher health benefits expense; G&A rose on increased professional fees.
EPS growth reflects net income up 34.4% q/q combined with a smaller diluted share count (66.1M vs 68.9M q/q) following $348M of quarterly share buybacks.
